get.description: Returns the comments on a task, paging through the whole history. ClickUp's upstream endpoint returns only the 25 newest comments per request and its response carries no total and no cursor, so this endpoint repeats the request with start/start_id until a page comes back short. Branch on `scan.complete`: false means comments remain unread, and `scan.nextStart` + `scan.nextStartId` are how to reach them. Threaded replies are not included.

parameters.name: taskId
parameters.description: The task ID

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum comments to return, newest first. Omit to return every comment on the task.

parameters.name: allPages
parameters.description: Set false to return only ClickUp's newest 25 comments (one upstream request). The response still reports scan.complete=false and a resume cursor.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Resume cursor: the `date` of the last comment of a previous response. Must be sent together with start_id; ClickUp ignores one without the other and returns the newest 25 again.

parameters.name: start_id
parameters.description: Resume cursor: the `id` of the last comment of a previous response. Must be sent together with start. `startId` is accepted as an alias.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Set to `text` (or send Accept: text/plain) for the markdown rendering instead of JSON.

200.description: Comments retrieved. Check scan.complete before treating the array as the whole history.

scan.description: Extent of the scan. `complete` is the field to branch on.

pageSize.description: Comments ClickUp returns per request (25). A page holding fewer is the only end-of-history signal the API gives.

complete.description: True only when a short page confirmed the end of the history. False means comments remain unread.

hitCap.description: Stopped at the internal page cap (40 pages / 1000 comments).

stalled.description: ClickUp returned the same page again for the next cursor, so paging could not advance.

rateLimited.description: ClickUp rate-limited the scan partway through; the pages already fetched are returned.

cursorUnavailable.description: The comment the next cursor had to be built from carried no id or date.

nextStart.description: Pass back as start to continue. Null when nothing remains or no cursor could be built.

nextStartId.description: Pass back as start_id to continue.

400.description: Unsupported query parameter (page/cursor), half a start/start_id cursor, contradictory start_id spellings, or a non-positive limit.

post.summary: Set a custom field value on a task
post.description: Sets the VALUE of an existing field. ClickUp has NO API to create a field or add a drop-down or label option, so the field and its options must already exist. Unlike the MCP tool this route forwards the value as-is: it does not resolve option names and does not revive a stringified array, so array-valued types (labels, users, relationships) must be sent as real JSON arrays or ClickUp answers FIELD_144 "Value must be an array".

post.summary: Update a task, or re-parent it
post.description: camelCase sibling of the legacy uncatalogued PATCH on /api/v1/clickup/tasks/{taskId}, which takes ClickUp-native keys instead. On the re-parent path the change is VERIFIED by a re-read, because ClickUp answers a parent change it silently ignores with HTTP 200 and emits no webhook for one: ALWAYS check reparentConfirmed. Removing a due date is clearDueDate: true — dueDate cannot express it. That clear is verified by a re-read too, so check dueDateCleared (true / false / null = unconfirmed).

parameters.name: taskId
parameters.description: The task ID

description.description: Plain text. markdownContent wins if both are sent.

markdownContent.description: Markdown body; takes precedence over description.

dueDate.description: ISO string or Unix ms. Include a time (2026-10-20T09:00:00Z) to set a due TIME; a bare date (2026-10-20) means the whole day, which ClickUp shows at 04:00 in the workspace timezone. To REMOVE an existing due date use clearDueDate — an empty string is refused as an invalid date.

clearDueDate.description: true removes the task's due date (ClickUp clears it on due_date: null). Cannot be combined with dueDate. Check dueDateCleared in the response: ClickUp answers an update it ignored with HTTP 200.

startDate.description: ISO string or Unix ms. Include a time to set a start TIME; a bare date means the whole day.

taskTypeId.description: 0 = Task, 1 = Milestone, or a workspace type. Changing it changes which custom fields apply, and therefore which are returned at all.

parentTaskId.description: Re-parent under this task. ClickUp CANNOT clear a parent, so null is refused with an explanation rather than sent.

reparentConfirmed.description: true = confirmed by a re-read. false = ClickUp accepted the call and silently ignored it, so do NOT treat the move as done. null = no re-parent requested, or the confirming read failed.

403.description: No ClickUp connection for this account, or permission denied

post.summary: Share a task into an additional list
post.description: Adds the task to a SECOND list while it stays in its current one. Use the move route to relocate it instead. Needs the "Tasks in Multiple Lists" ClickApp, and ClickUp answers a DISABLED ClickApp with 401 — the same status as a bad credential, so a 401 here does not mean your token is wrong. ClickUp answers 200 with an EMPTY body, so the task is re-read for evidence: confirmed is three-valued because a payload carrying no locations array (what a disabled ClickApp looks like) is not evidence of absence. Unlike the MCP tool this route runs no pre-flight.

parameters.description: The task ID

parameters.name: listId
parameters.description: The list ID

confirmed.description: true = the re-read agrees. false = it disagrees. null = ClickUp sent no locations array, so the outcome is unverified, NOT failed.

homeListId.description: ClickUp cannot remove a task from its home list.

locations.description: Additional list IDs, when ClickUp reported them.
